messages:
maria: seeing a weird pattern in us-west-2 last hour — some tenants hit 503 while dedicated pools had spare slots. suspect spillback windowing + preempt window mismatch. logs: AllocReject Err=NO_CAPACITY region=us-west-2 pool=shared-rt

ajay: can you paste the rollup of allocations? did the router fall back to shared at t=... ?

maria: paste logs snippet:
```
2024-11-03T15:22:11Z router: fallback start tenant=acme-corp reason=reserved_full
2024-11-03T15:22:11Z alloc: queued tenant=acme-corp pref=dedicated->shared
2024-11-03T15:22:12Z serve: preempt_request tenant=beta-app target=dedicated-42 state=denied
```

sophie: oncall saw correlating NIC drops and egress queuing in that AZ — might be network-induced longer tails causing scheduler to think nodes are slower and preempt more? :thinking_face:

kevin: if preempt window is shorter than spillback cooldown we get flip-flopping: router pushes to shared then preempt returns capacity and router tries to move back -> churn and cost shift. we should add a 30s prefer-stability hold, or at least a backoff with hysteresis.

maria: agree, also cost shift: shared pools billed at spot rate but bursting to dedicated while billing still shows dedicated commit — customers see higher unit cost. ops reported $12k unexpected for that day.

ajay: proposed actions: 1) instrument router for roll-forward/backoff counters 2) bump preempt window to 90s for us-west-2 for immediate mitigation 3) add a short (20s) spillback hold in routing policy 4) run a canary with acme-corp flag tomorrow 08:00 PT

sophie: doing 2 & 3 now on canary stack. will watch latency and token/sec. will pause if error rate >1% for 10m. pinging @infra-sre for capacity check.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT_NOTE: started canary for spillback-hold at 2024-11-03T16:05:00Z — watcher=sophie

kevin: also we should run a cost-recalc job to attribute those bursts to tenants for billing reconciliation.

maria: thanks all. action owners: ajay=router metrics, sophie=canary, kevin=billing job. I'll file a follow-up postmortem if we still see churn after 48h.

ajay: I'll add a metrics dashboard: 'router.spillback.count', 'router.hold.seconds', 'preempt.flip_flop' and set alerts.

sophie: canary shows improvement after 5m: 503s down from 0.9% -> 0.1%. leaving canary running 1h.

maria: marking as resolved for now, will reopen if spike >0.5% again. :white_check_mark:
